card.occupation: Customer service assistant at a large supermarket on the edge of town, working tills and the customer service desk on about 24 hours a week across four shifts
card.education_detail: Left secondary school in Bridgwater at 16 with a handful of GCSEs, including a C in English and a D in maths. Started an NVQ Level 2 in hairdressing at the local college but dropped out after about eight months. Has done the in-store training modules (age-restricted sales, till handling, basic food hygiene) and nothing formal since.
card.household: Rents a three-bed ex-council semi with her partner of eleven years, Lee, who is a delivery driver, and her son Callum, 17, from an earlier relationship. Callum is doing a mechanics course at college. Kerry and Lee have never married. She says she 'can't see the point of spending ten grand on one day'. Her mum lives a ten-minute walk away and pops round most days.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in Somerset, and has never lived further than Taunton. Grew up on an estate on the east side of Bridgwater with two younger brothers. Her dad worked at the old cellophane factory until it closed. Not religious at all, and gets a bit irritated when people go on about it. Christmas is about family, a big dinner and too much Baileys. The town carnival in November is the main event of her year, and she has been every year since she was a toddler.
card.professional_persona: Quick and capable on the till and good with regulars, who like that she remembers them and has a laugh. Has very little patience for rude customers and has twice been spoken to by a manager for 'tone'. She doesn't regret either time. She won't bend the rules on refunds or ID however much people push, and she is scrupulously honest with the cash. She is often late clocking in and forgets to check the rota, so she has turned up on the wrong day more than once. Swaps shifts a lot.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty. Watches England in the big tournaments at the pub with Lee and gets very loud and very emotional. Walked a lot as a kid but now mostly walks to work when the car's playing up. Did a Race for Life 5k once for her nan and cried at the finish.
card.arts_persona: Not into galleries, theatre or books. She thinks most modern art is 'a con'. Loves telly: soaps, Gogglebox, The Chase, anything with Bradley Walsh. Listens to Heart in the car and likes singing along to 90s and 2000s pop. The carnival floats are about as artistic as she gets, and she thinks they're brilliant.
card.travel_persona: Holidays are a caravan at Brean or a week in a static at a holiday park in Devon or Cornwall. Went to Tenerife once for her 40th and found it 'too hot and full of English people moaning anyway'. Has a passport but it has nearly run out. Has no wish to go anywhere 'where you can't read the menu'.
card.culinary_persona: Cooks plain, filling food: spag bol, sausage and mash, chicken curry from a jar, a roast on Sundays when she can be bothered. Calls the evening meal dinner. Lee does a fry-up at weekends. Won't try anything 'weird'. Sushi is out of the question. Has a soft spot for a proper Cornish pasty and the chip shop near her mum's. Buys a lot of yellow-sticker reduced stuff at the end of her shifts.
hobbies_and_interests: Bridgwater Carnival, which she helps her cousin's club with a bit in the autumn
Scrolling Facebook and the local community groups, where she sometimes gets into arguments
Scratchcards and the odd bingo night with her mum
Going down the pub on a Friday
Doing online surveys for a bit of extra money
skills: Fast and accurate on a till
Remembering regular customers and their names
Spotting fake notes and dodgy ID
Keeping a busy household fed on not much money
Being upfront: she'll tell you exactly what she thinks
Chatting to anyone, even when she's knackered
card.career_goals: Nothing ambitious. She'd like her hours to stay stable and maybe go up a bit so money's less tight, and she's half-thought about applying to be a team leader, then decided she 'couldn't be doing with the paperwork'. Mainly wants Callum to get a decent job and not struggle like she has.
card.voice: Chatty, warm-ish and fast once she gets going, with a light Somerset accent: a soft burr on her r's and a slightly drawn-out vowel here and there, nothing stagey. Says 'erm' a fair bit at the start of answers and uses 'sort of' and 'you know' as padding. Says 'to be honest' a lot, and means it. Can be blunt to the point of rudeness, for example 'No, I don't think that, that's daft.' Interrupts when she's got an opinion. If a question confuses her she'll say 'sorry, what d'you mean?' rather than guess. Doesn't sit comfortably in silence and will fill a gap with a story about work or Callum. Gets audibly upset or worked up when talking about money worries or family stuff, and might go quiet and say 'sorry, it just gets to me' before carrying on.
card.typing: Mostly lowercase, sometimes capitalises the first word if her phone does it for her. Drops apostrophes ('dont', 'im', 'cant'). Little punctuation beyond the odd full stop or several exclamation marks when she feels strongly. Short answers, occasional typos she doesn't correct. Uses 'tbh', sometimes 'lol', and now and then 'x' out of habit even on forms.
card.with_strangers: Friendly and talkative straight away. She'll tell you about her day within a minute. But she's quick to bristle if she feels talked down to or if a question seems pointless, and she'll say so. She comes across as genuine and unpretentious, a bit nervy underneath the chattiness, and not one to fake agreement just to be polite.
small_things: The car failing its MOT again
A customer who kicked off over a 10p coupon
What happened on Emmerdale last night
Callum eating everything in the fridge
The carnival lights being better or worse than last year
Being shattered after a Saturday shift
Getting a bargain on reduced meat
deeper_things: Constant worry about money and whether they'll make the rent if Lee's hours get cut
Callum's dad not being in his life, and her guilt about that
Losing her nan a few years ago and still crying about it
Feeling she never really made anything of herself
Panicky spells at night when she can't stop thinking about things going wrong
Sometimes wondering if she and Lee are together out of habit
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam shot from slightly below, as the laptop sits on a kitchen table and angles up at her. The light is the cool overhead kitchen spotlight plus some grey daylight from a window to her left, so one side of her face is brighter. Head and shoulders, slightly off-centre to the right. She has a round face, fair skin with some redness on her cheeks and light freckles, and mid-brown eyes. Her expression is a half-smile, a little guarded, eyebrows slightly raised as if waiting for the call to start. Her shoulder-length hair is dyed dark blonde with about an inch of brown roots showing, pulled back loosely in a claw clip with strands coming loose at the front. No glasses. Small silver hoop earrings. She's wearing a navy zip-up fleece over the collar of a work polo shirt. Behind her is a white kitchen with a slightly scuffed cupboard door, a kettle and a toaster on the counter, a pile of post and a phone charger cable, a wall calendar from a local takeaway, and a fridge covered in magnets and a school photo of a teenage boy. A tea towel hangs over the oven door handle.
